Percentage.introduction: Percentage represents a quantity as a fraction of 100.
concepts: To find x% of a number, multiply it by x/100.
Percentage change is calculated relative to the original value.
important: Convert fractions into percentages by multiplying by 100.
Always use the original value when calculating percentage change.

Profit and Loss.introduction: Profit and loss measure financial gain or loss in a transaction.
concepts: Profit percentage is calculated using cost price.
Profit and Loss.example: Cost price = 400 and selling price = 500. Profit = 100. Profit percentage = 25%.
important: Cost price is the purchasing price.
Selling price determines the profit or loss.

Logical Reasoning.description: Improve logical thinking and analytical abilities.

Number Series.introduction: Number series questions require identifying patterns in sequences.
concepts: Look for multiplication or division patterns.
Number Series.formula: Next term = Previous term + Common Difference
important: Check whether the difference is constant.
Look for square, cube and prime number patterns.

Coding and Decoding.introduction: Coding and decoding questions use systematic transformations of letters.
concepts: Letters may be shifted forward or backward.
Coding and Decoding.example: CAT becomes DBU by shifting each letter one position forward.

Data Interpretation.description: Interpret numerical information using tables and graphs.

Bar Graphs.introduction: Bar graphs compare values across different categories.
concepts: Compare bar heights using the vertical scale.
Bar Graphs.example: Sales increase from 100 to 150 units. Percentage increase = 50%.
important: Always check the scale of the graph.
Distinguish absolute difference from percentage difference.

Pie Charts.introduction: Pie charts represent proportions of a whole.
concepts: A complete pie chart represents 360 degrees.
Each sector represents a proportion of the total.
Sector angles can be converted into percentages.
Pie Charts.example: A sector of 90 degrees represents 25% of the total.
important: All sector angles must add up to 360 degrees.
Use the total value when calculating proportions.

Operating Systems.introduction: An operating system manages computer hardware and software resources.
Operating Systems.formula: CPU Utilization = (CPU Busy Time / Total Time) × 100
Operating Systems.example: Windows, Linux and macOS are examples of operating systems.
important: The operating system acts as an interface between users and hardware.
Process scheduling determines which process receives CPU time.

Database Management.introduction: A DBMS stores, organizes and manages structured information.
concepts: Foreign keys establish relationships between tables.
Database Management.formula: A relational table consists of attributes (columns) and tuples (rows).
Database Management.example: A student table may contain Student_ID, Name and Department.
important: A primary key uniquely identifies a record.
